title: Lawn grub treatment
subtitle: Based on official Australian sources, Mitch's past jobs and the product labels, checked against NSW requirements. Mitch will show you his own method on the ride-along. Updated 6 Nov 2026.

sections.heading: When this job comes up
body: Customer has lawn grubs in their lawn. Mitch's service is called Lawn Grub Treatment. Past invoices read: "Lawn grub treatment using registered insecticide" with the lawn area in square metres, and "Larvae Treatment, cottage only".
In a lawn the damage usually comes from curl grubs (beetle grubs that eat the roots) or lawn armyworm (caterpillars that eat the leaves). Check which one it is before you treat.
The job process, the never list, PPE and the free service period are in the Every job guide.

sections.heading: What the law and the label require

items.text: Follow the product label
items.detail: Using a pesticide against its label is an offence. If the job needs something the label does not allow, stop and call Mitch.

items.text: Make the record the same day
items.detail: Every pesticide job needs a record: full product name, date, target pest, rate and quantity, address and area treated, who applied it, equipment, and start and finish times. It must be made within 48 hours and kept at least 3 years. Give the customer a copy if they ask.

items.text: Outdoor spraying: record the weather
items.detail: Write down wind speed and direction at the start and whenever it changes. Add temperature, humidity or rain if the label says it matters. A subfloor outside the walls counts as outdoors.

items.text: Keep it out of waterways
items.detail: Never spray near waterways, ponds, tanks or fish. Check the label for the distance.

items.text: Only do work your licence covers
items.detail: If a treatment is outside your licence class, work under Mitch's direct supervision and do not do it alone.

items.text: Protect people, pets and the environment
items.detail: Wear the PPE the label and SDS call for. Keep spray and bait away from people, pets, food, drains and waterways. Harming people, wildlife or property with a pesticide is an offence.

sections.heading: How to tell what is eating the lawn
rows: Large white or cream C-shaped grub with a brown head and six legs near the head. Lives in the soil and eats the roots.
Plants with eaten roots can wilt or go yellow. Dead grass pulls up easily. Birds digging at the lawn can be the first sign.
A curl grub, about 25 mm when fully grown, with a brown or tan head. The adult is a glossy brown-black beetle about 14 mm.
A real problem in newly sown lawns. The adults fly in late summer and autumn.
Smooth, plump caterpillar up to about 40 mm, greyish brown with pale and dark markings. Hides at the base of the grass or under soil clods in the day, feeds at night.
Leaves stripped and bare patches, with green-yellow pellet droppings.
Dry or hungry grass can look the same. Rule these out before you blame grubs.
Looks like grub damage. Grubs are unlikely to do real damage unless there are lots of them.

items.text: Rule out dry or hungry grass first
Tug the dead grass
items.detail: If it lifts out easily, the roots have probably been eaten.

items.text: Dig a small patch at the edge of the damage and look in the top of the soil and the roots for white C-shaped grubs
Look at the base of the grass and under soil clods for caterpillars, or look at dusk when they come out
Kids and pets off the lawn. Pet bowls and bedding moved
Cover fish ponds, barbecues and vegie gardens near the lawn. Close doors and windows
Rainwater tank: stop overspray getting onto the gutters and roof
Not on a rainy or windy day
items.detail: Follow the label's weather limits.

sections.heading: PPE
sections.title: PPE on before you go in
sections.note: Never apply chemicals without PPE. If the SDS requires it, you wear it. No exceptions.
items: Gloves and closed shoes at minimum
Gloves, mask and eye protection for any spray, as per the product SDS

sections.heading: Products Mitch uses
sections.title: Names as in Mitch's product list. No rates here: follow the label. Use the product Mitch has loaded, after checking its label covers lawn grubs and this lawn.
rows: Country Bifenthrin 100 Low Odour Termiticide & Insecticide

sections.heading: Steps
sections.title: Steps
sections.note: How to check it is grubs and the spraying precautions are from official sources and are marked. How Mitch treats the lawn is still to confirm.
items: Ask the customer to show you where the lawn is damaged
Take BEFORE photos of the damaged areas

items.text: Check it really is grubs (see How to check)
items.detail: Dry or hungry grass can look the same.

items.text: Work out the lawn area in square metres
items.detail: Past invoices give the area in m2. Mitch will show you how he measures it.

items.text: Estimate the wind speed and direction before you start, and write it down. Note it again if the wind changes
items.detail: Outdoor spraying needs this in the record, and anything else the label says about weather.

items.text: Treat the lawn
items.detail: Apply with the power spray rig as the label directs. Follow the label on watering in. Do not water the garden after spraying, and check the label for how long to wait.

items.text: Apply per the product label. Never exceed label rates
items.detail: Never mix chemicals without checking the label first. If in doubt, call Mitch.

items: Keep chemicals away from food, children and pets
Note anything you could not treat or reach, and why

sections.heading: Job complete when
items: Lawn area treated as agreed with Mitch, and the area in square metres written on the job report
Anything you could not treat or reach is noted on the job report, with the reason

items.text: Product, rate, area and quantity recorded on the job report, plus the wind speed and direction
items.detail: The record is made within 48 hours and kept for 3 years.

items: Customer told what you did and what to expect (see "If the customer asks" below)
Customer told when to water: follow the product label
Customer given the re-entry time: follow the product label. The Every job guide says 1 to 2 hours once dry
Service report left, or customer told it is being emailed

items.a: Often it's one of two things. Curl grubs are beetle grubs that live in the soil and eat the roots. Lawn armyworm are caterpillars that eat the leaves. We check which one you've got.

items.q: Why did the lawn go so fast?
items.a: Armyworm hide at the base of the grass in the day and feed at night, so you don't see them until the patches show.

items.q: When can the kids and the dog go back on the lawn?
items.a: Keep them off while we treat. Follow the product label for when it's safe. We normally say 1 to 2 hours once it's dry.
Follow the product label. Don't water straight after spraying unless the label says to.
It depends how much has been eaten. A good feed and water helps it recover, once the label says it's okay to water.

items.q: Why did you want to move the job for rain or wind?
items.a: Spraying outdoors on a rainy or windy day isn't recommended, so we pick a better day.

sections.heading: Tell Mitch straight away if
sections.body: Call Mitch on 0432 181 689. After hours or urgent, call Mitch directly.

items.text: You apply the wrong chemical
items.detail: Stop immediately. Do not continue. Call Mitch.

items.text: There is a spill
items.detail: Follow the SDS procedure. Call Mitch immediately. Never leave a spill unattended.

items.text: Someone is hurt
items.detail: Treat the injury first. Call Mitch. Write down what happened.

items.text: The customer complains or gets aggressive
items.detail: Stay calm and do not argue. For a complaint, tell them Mitch will call them today. If they are aggressive, remove yourself. Call Mitch either way.

items.text: The customer asks for a quote on anything complex, or you are not sure
items.detail: Say "I'll need to get Mitch to come and have a look and provide a quote for that."

items.text: You see signs of termites or other pests outside this job
items.detail: Photograph it and tell Mitch. Termite quotes always go to Mitch.
